ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence gives your own name? (1 mark)
   A. maa ismuka?
   B. maʿa s-salaama
   C. kayfa haaluka?
   D. ismii Ahmad

2. Which Arabic word means "and upon you peace (the reply)"? (1 mark)
   A. أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ
   B. كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟
   C. مَرْحَبًا
   D. وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ

3. What does the ending -ii mean in abii and ummii? (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. my
   C. our
   D. his

4. What does the Arabic sentence أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I like bananas.
   B. I like juice.
   C. I eat bread.
   D. I drink water.

5. What does ilmis anfaka tell you to do? (1 mark)
   A. Raise your hand
   B. Close your eyes
   C. Open your mouth
   D. Touch your nose

6. How is the Arabic word رَقَبَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. wajh
   B. raqaba
   C. isbaʿ
   D. yad

7. What does the Arabic word عَيْنٌ (ʿayn) mean? (1 mark)
   A. eye
   B. hand
   C. hair
   D. tongue

8. Which Arabic sentence means "Thank you for listening." (1 mark)
   A. شُكْرًا لِاسْتِمَاعِكُمْ
   B. أَنَا فِي الصَّفِّ الرَّابِعِ
   C. آكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ
   D. فِي بَيْتِي مَطْبَخٌ

9. What is the name of the Arabic letter غ? (1 mark)
   A. baa
   B. faa
   C. Saad
   D. ghayn

10. What is the name of the Arabic letter ج? (1 mark)
   A. jiim
   B. qaaf
   C. dhaal
   D. faa

11. How many letters are in the Arabic alphabet? (1 mark)
   A. 28
   B. 24
   C. 30
   D. 26

12. How do you read the syllable بُ? (1 mark)
   A. thaa
   B. laa
   C. du
   D. bu

13. What does the Arabic sentence عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   B. The house is big.
   C. In the kitchen there is a table.
   D. On the table there is a cup.

14. Which Arabic sentence means "The house is big." (1 mark)
   A. فِي الْمَطْبَخِ طَاوِلَةٌ وَكُرْسِيٌّ
   B. الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ
   C. عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ
   D. أَزْرَعُ شَجَرَةً

15. What does the Arabic sentence أُسَاعِدُ أُمِّي يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I help my mother on Saturday.
   B. I visit my grandmother on Friday.
   C. I read a book on Sunday.
   D. I like juice.

16. Which Arabic word means "dance"? (1 mark)
   A. هَدِيَّةٌ
   B. رَقْصٌ
   C. حَفْلَةٌ
   D. كَعْكَةٌ

17. What are verbal cues? (1 mark)
   A. The number of pages
   B. The size of letters
   C. The colour of the page
   D. Intonation, speed and tonal variation

18. Which of these Arabic words (in English letters) means 'clouds'? (1 mark)
   A. shams
   B. riih
   C. matar
   D. ghaym

19. Which Arabic word means "cold"? (1 mark)
   A. بَارِدٌ
   B. حَارٌّ
   C. رِيحٌ
   D. سَحَابٌ

20. What does the word min mean in maTaru mina s-samaa'i? (1 mark)
   A. in
   B. from
   C. on
   D. and

21. Which sound does the Arabic letter ل make? (1 mark)
   A. m as in mat
   B. b as in bag
   C. l as in lamp
   D. kh, a throat sound like the ch in loch

22. Which sound does the Arabic letter ن make? (1 mark)
   A. j as in jug
   B. f as in fan
   C. n as in net
   D. d as in dog

23. What is the name of the Arabic letter ث? (1 mark)
   A. DHaa
   B. Saad
   C. haa
   D. thaa

24. What does the shadda over the last letter of umm tell the reader? (1 mark)
   A. The letter is silent
   B. Say the letter twice
   C. The word is finished
   D. The vowel is long

25. Which of these is a masculine noun? (1 mark)
   A. qitta (cat)
   B. taawila (table)
   C. kursii (chair)
   D. naafidha (window)

26. How is the Arabic word لَذِيذٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. baarid
   B. as-salaamu ʿalaykum
   C. taawila
   D. ladhiidh

27. Which Arabic word means "drink"? (1 mark)
   A. شَرَابٌ
   B. شَمْعَةٌ
   C. عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ
   D. صَدِيقٌ

28. Which describing word matches yad (hand), which is feminine? (1 mark)
   A. Sagiira
   B. kabiir
   C. qawiyy
   D. jadiid

29. What does the Arabic sentence رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My head is big.
   B. I wash my face.
   C. I clean my teeth.
   D. My hand is small.

30. What does the Arabic sentence الشَّمْسُ حَارَّةٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is rain.
   B. The sun is hot.
   C. This is the sun.
   D. The wind is strong.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Translate into English: ummii tatbukhu (2 marks)

32. Explain why dots are important in Arabic letters. Give an example. (3 marks) (3 marks)

33. Write the Arabic sounds for 'two hands' and 'two legs' and give the meaning of each ending. (3 marks) (3 marks)

34. Name three rooms of the house in Arabic (English letters) with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

35. Translate into English: fii l-usbuuʿi sabʿatu ayyaam (2 marks)

36. Translate into English: nahnu narqusu (2 marks)

37. Write five words about a celebration in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

38. Explain how the same Arabic word can look different but keep its meaning. (2 marks) (2 marks)

39. Translate into English: anaa ʿinda l-baab (2 marks)

40. Translate into English: as-samaku ladhiidh (2 marks)

41. Write one Arabic sentence about a household item using a describing word, and translate it. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Describe two things you can do to pronounce the days of the week correctly. (2 marks) (2 marks)

43. Spell the word باب by naming the letters in order, and give its meaning. (3 marks) (3 marks)

44. Write three classroom instructions in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

45. Explain the difference between kayfa haaluka? and kayfa haaluki? (2 marks) (2 marks)

46. Explain why you should copy sounds carefully when learning Arabic words. (2 marks) (2 marks)

47. Translate into English: haadhihi yadii (2 marks)

48. Translate into English: kulla ʿaamin wa-antum bi-khayr (2 marks)

49. Give three items from a peer review checklist for reading aloud. (3 marks) (3 marks)

50. Translate into English: anaa min Kiiniya (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — ismii Ahmad
   ismii means 'my name is', so ismii Ahmad means 'My name is Ahmad'.

2. D — وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ
   وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ (wa ʿalaykumu s-salaam) means and upon you peace (the reply).

3. B — my
   The ending -ii means 'my', so abii is 'my father' and ummii is 'my mother'.

4. A — I like bananas.
   أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ (uhibbu l-mawza) means: I like bananas.

5. D — Touch your nose
   ilmis means touch and anfaka means your nose.

6. B — raqaba
   رَقَبَةٌ is read raqaba and means neck.

7. A — eye
   عَيْنٌ (ʿayn) means eye.

8. A — شُكْرًا لِاسْتِمَاعِكُمْ
   شُكْرًا لِاسْتِمَاعِكُمْ (shukran li-istimaaʿikum) means: Thank you for listening.

9. D — ghayn
   The letter غ is called ghayn.

10. A — jiim
   The letter ج is called jiim.

11. A — 28
   The Arabic alphabet has 28 letters.

12. D — bu
   بُ is read bu.

13. D — On the table there is a cup.
   عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ (ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub) means: On the table there is a cup.

14. B — الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ
   الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ (al-baytu kabiir) means: The house is big.

15. A — I help my mother on Saturday.
   أُسَاعِدُ أُمِّي يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ (usaaʿidu ummii yawma s-sabt) means: I help my mother on Saturday.

16. B — رَقْصٌ
   رَقْصٌ (raqs) means dance.

17. D — Intonation, speed and tonal variation
   Verbal cues are the ways the voice shows meaning.

18. D — ghaym
   ghaym means clouds.

19. A — بَارِدٌ
   بَارِدٌ (baarid) means cold.

20. B — from
   min means 'from', so 'the rain is from the sky'.

21. C — l as in lamp
   The letter ل makes the sound l as in lamp.

22. C — n as in net
   The letter ن makes the sound n as in net.

23. D — thaa
   The letter ث is called thaa.

24. B — Say the letter twice
   A shadda doubles the sound.

25. C — kursii (chair)
   kursii is masculine. The other words end in -a and are feminine.

26. D — ladhiidh
   لَذِيذٌ is read ladhiidh and means delicious.

27. A — شَرَابٌ
   شَرَابٌ (sharaab) means drink.

28. A — Sagiira
   yad is feminine, so it takes the describing word ending in -a.

29. A — My head is big.
   رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ (raʾsii kabiir) means: My head is big.

30. B — The sun is hot.
   الشَّمْسُ حَارَّةٌ (ash-shamsu haarra) means: The sun is hot.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: My mother cooks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some letters have the same body shape and differ only by their dots. For example baa has one dot below, taa has two dots above and thaa has three dots above.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for same shape, 1 mark for dots make the difference and 1 mark for a correct example.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: yadaani (two hands) and rijlaani (two legs). The ending -aani means two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word and 1 mark for the ending.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example ghurfa (room), matbakh (kitchen), hammaam (bathroom), hadiiqa (garden).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning, up to 3.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: There are seven days in a week.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: We dance.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example ʿiid (festival), hafla (party), hadiyya (gift), baaluun (balloon), kaʿka (cake).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: In different writing styles the letter shapes change a little, but the letters, sounds and meaning stay the same.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for shapes change and 1 mark for meaning stays the same.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am at the door.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: The fish is delicious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example al-baabu kabiir. The door is big.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence, 1 mark for a matching describing word and 1 mark for the translation.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the teacher and repeat; say the days in a chain; practise the sounds th and kh slowly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid method.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: baa, alif, baa. It means door.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the letters, 1 mark for the order and 1 mark for the meaning.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example qif (stand up), ijlis (sit down), iftahi l-baab (open the door).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct instruction with meaning.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: kayfa haaluka? is said to a boy or man. kayfa haaluki? is said to a girl or woman. Both mean 'How are you?'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the boy and girl endings and 1 mark for the meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: A small change in a sound can change the meaning, and careful copying makes you clear to the listener.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for change of meaning and 1 mark for being understood.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my hand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: May you be well every year.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Every word read correctly; steady pace; voice rises for questions; pauses at commas; voice shows feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid item.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am from Kenya.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.
